headlines.title: Apple back-to-school sale: Save up to 34% on Macbooks, AirPods and more
headlines.description: Apple products rarely go on sale, but right now several are up to 34% off for back-to-school season. Shop deals on laptops, iPads, AirPods and more.

headlines.title: Bumble scraps signature rule and now allows men to make first move on dating app
headlines.description: Dating app Bumble announced on Tuesday that it would be getting rid of its hallmark rule that prevents men from making the first move.

headlines.title: Why is the U.S. banning a ton of robot vacuums? Here’s what you should know
headlines.description: The FCC banned foreign-made advanced robots, and robot vacuums fall under the new rules. Here’s what it means for the device you already own — and which models you can still buy.

headlines.title: Excitement Builds Across Europe for Rare Total Solar Eclipse
headlines.description: Excitement is building across Europe ahead of the continent’s first total solar eclipse in more than 25 years. The sun will be completely covered by the moon for just one minute and 43 seconds, but it is long enough to attract nearly half a million tourists who will be gazing skyward. NBC’s Raf Sanchez reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Crowley thanks supporters after winning Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor
headlines.description: David Crowley spoke to supporters after pulling off a win in a close Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor against Francesca Hong.

headlines.title: Meta A.I. glasses spark privacy concerns as women report being recorded without consent
headlines.description: Meta A.I. glasses draw growing backlash on social media as more people, mostly women, speak out about being filmed, with the videos being posted online without their consent. NBC News’ Yasmin Vossoughian reports on the debate where privacy laws and technology collide.

headlines.title: Easy AI Hacks to Help Improve Your Day-to-Day Life
headlines.description: Futurist and tech entrepreneur Sinead Bovell joins TODAY’s Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones to share simple AI life hacks you can start using today. Her tips include using the technology to give you personalized home organization tips, outfit advice, and more.

headlines.title: French Rejection: How France is Hanging Up on Telemarketers
headlines.description: Lawmakers in France have passed a new law that bans unsolicited marketing calls. Instead of opting out to avoid those unwanted calls, consumers can only receive a call from companies if they opt in. Violators will be fined the equivalent of $435,000 per call. Meanwhile, lawmakers in the United States are also looking to tackle the issue with numerous bills in the works. NBC’s Joe Fryer reports for TODAY.

headlines.title: Job applicants use hidden text to trick A.I. screeners
headlines.description: Some job seekers are reportedly using hidden text in their resumes and applications to trick A.I. hiring systems. Developer Relations Engineer and content creator Harnoor Singh breaks down the potential impact this has for applicants.

headlines.title: Make the Most of Every Inch of Space With These Products
headlines.description: Small spaces can get cluttered easily, so Shop TODAY fashion and lifestyle contributor Chassie Post breaks down her favorite products to maximize your storage. See her recommendations, which include under bed storage with wheels, a bathroom tool organizer, and more!

headlines.title: Flock cameras vandalized across the country as the debate around them continues
headlines.description: Communities across the country are debating whether or not they should keep using controversial Flock Safety cameras as a number of them are vandalized. Police say the cameras help them track down criminals, but critics say they’re an invasion of privacy. NBC News’ Dana Griffin reports.

headlines.title: Teenage boys are obsessing over luxury colognes in a new trend known as ‘smellmaxxing’
headlines.description: For some teen boys’ back-to-school shopping, a new item has been added to the list: cologne. The social media trend known as ‘smellmaxxing’ has young boys layering different scents and spending hundreds of dollars on luxury bottles. NBC News’ Valerie Castro takes a look at the growing trend.
